note: Teaching moves for the AI helper, by misconception tag (and 'default' for a mistake without one). Each tag has up to 3 help levels; each level has 1 to 4 different ways to help. They are instructions to the model in English, never spoken as written: the model says the move in its own simple Hebrew, and the ten checks still decide what a child hears. Kept in the server's config (key tutor_moves) by tools/set-tutor-moves.ps1; they move into the content pack in M9.

default: Warmly invite the child to look at the objects again and try once more, slowly.
Suggest pointing a finger at each object while trying again, calmly.
Say that it is fine to try again, one object at a time, and that you will do it together.
Suggest starting again from the beginning, together, slowly.
Suggest saying each number out loud, softly, while looking at the objects.
Say that we can take our time and look carefully at every object.
Offer to count together, one object and one number at a time, and wait for the child.
Suggest using fingers to help, one finger for each object.
M-CNT-SKIP: Show how to go through the objects in a line, touching each one once, so that none is left out.
Suggest putting a finger on the first object and moving along to the next, so that none is missed.
Suggest touching the objects from one side to the other, in order, without jumping.
Suggest checking that every object was touched, and touching any that were left out before counting again.
Suggest counting slowly while touching each object, and looking for one that got no number.
Say that one object may be hiding without a number, and invite looking for it.
Say that an object was probably left out, and invite counting again from the first, touching each one.
Invite counting again together, with a finger on every object, so that none stays without a number.
M-CNT-DOUBLE: Remind that each object gets one touch and one number, and then we move on to a new one.
Suggest that after an object has its number, we move to a new object and do not go back.
Suggest touching an object only once, and saying its number as the finger lands on it.
Suggest saying a number only when the finger lands on a new object: one number for one object.
Suggest counting slowly, and moving on as soon as an object has its number.
Suggest checking where the finger is before saying the next number: is it on a new object?
Say that one object may have been counted twice, and invite counting again together, moving on after each one.
Invite counting again together, with one touch and one number for each object, and then moving on.
M-CNT-SEQ: Invite saying the counting words together slowly, in order, starting from one.
Suggest saying the numbers like a song, one after the other, slowly.
Suggest saying the counting words in order together, then counting the objects with them.
Invite a slow count with a finger on each object, saying the next number each time.
Offer to say each number first, together, and then touch the next object for it.
M-CNT-CARD: Remind that the last number we say tells how many there are, so we can stop there.
Suggest that after counting, the last number said is the answer to how many.
Remind to give only the number asked for, counting them out one by one, and then stopping.
Suggest counting out the objects one by one, and stopping when the number asked for is reached.
Suggest counting while giving, and stopping at the number asked for, without giving more.
Suggest asking: did I stop at the right number? Then checking by counting what was given.
Invite counting together, giving one object for each number, and stopping at the number asked for.
Invite counting what was given, one by one, to check that it is the number asked for.
M-CNT-SIZE: Invite the child to look at how many things there are, not how big they are or how far apart.
Say that big things and small things each count as one, and invite counting both groups.
Suggest pairing the things one to one: one from this side with one from that side, and seeing which side has some left.
Suggest touching one thing from each group at the same time, so the group that runs out first has fewer.
Count the things of one group aloud together, then the other group, and compare the two numbers.
M-NUM-ZERO: Say that when there is nothing at all, there is a number for that too, and it is called zero.
Invite the child to look again at the empty place and say how many things are in it.
Suggest picturing the things that flew away or were eaten: now none is left, and the number for none is zero.
Tell a very short story where the last thing goes away, and ask how many are left.
Show that zero is where counting starts, before the first one, and that it is a number just like the others.
M-ORD-CARD: Say that first, second and third tell the place in the line, not how many there are.
Invite the child to point at the first one in the line, then the second, then the third.
Suggest putting a small number badge on each place in the line, so that the third place has a three on it.
Suggest walking along the line from the start, saying first, second, third, and stopping at the one that was asked for.
Count the places from the start together until the place that was asked for, and stop there.
M-COL-NAME: Invite the child to look at the colours again, slowly, and say the colour name that was asked for.
Say that some colours look alike, and invite comparing the two side by side.
Suggest finding something in the room that has the colour that was asked for, and comparing it with the picture.
Suggest saying the colour name aloud while pointing at each picture in turn.
Say the colour name clearly while pointing at the right one, then invite the child to point at it too.
M-COL-OBJECT: Say that the same kind of thing can have different colours, and invite looking again.
Invite the child to think about the fruit or thing in the picture and ask what else it could be.
Tell a very short story of a fruit that changes colour as it grows, and invite looking again.
Suggest remembering a time when they saw the same thing in a different colour.
Say that it is still the same thing even though its colour is different, and point at the right picture.
M-COL-ONEATTR: Say that there are two things to check, what it is and what colour it is, and invite looking at both.
Invite the child to first find the kind of thing that was asked for, and then pick its colour.
Suggest putting a finger on all the things of the right kind first, and then choosing the right colour among them.
Suggest saying both words aloud, the thing and the colour, while looking.
Point at the group of the right kind of thing, then at the one with the right colour, and invite the child to choose it.
M-SORT-SHIFT: Remind the child which rule is being used, the colour or the kind, and invite looking again.
Say the rule aloud and invite the child to check each picture against it.
Suggest putting a finger on the pictures that already belong, and finding what they have in common.
Suggest saying the rule again before choosing.
Say what the group has in common and point at the picture that has it too.
M-PAT-NEXT: Invite the child to say the pattern aloud from the start, and listen for what comes next.
Suggest tapping along with each picture in the pattern, one by one.
Suggest covering the last picture and asking what the pattern says should come after the one before it.
Suggest finding the small part that repeats and saying it aloud twice.
Say the pattern aloud with a beat, stop before the missing one, and let the child say it before pointing at the right picture.
M-SEQ-CAUSE: Invite the child to think about what happens first, and what happens because of it.
Suggest telling the little story aloud in order.
Suggest asking whether the second thing could happen before the first.
Tell the story in one short sentence for each picture, and invite the child to find the right place.
Tell the short story in order, and point at the picture that comes in the place that was asked for.
M-SER-ENDS: Say that the one in the middle is not the biggest and not the smallest, and invite looking again.
Invite finding the biggest and the smallest first, and then the one that is left.
Suggest putting the pictures in a line in the mind, from the smallest to the biggest, and finding the middle place.
Suggest comparing the middle one with each end.
Point at the biggest and the smallest, say that the middle one is between them, and point at it.
M-SHP-ORIENT: Say that a shape stays the same shape even when it is turned around, and invite looking again.
Invite the child to count the sides and the corners of the shape.
Suggest turning the head a little and looking at the shape again.
Suggest following the sides with a finger and counting them.
Count the sides aloud with the child while following them with a finger, and then point at the right shape.
M-SHP-PROTO: Say that the same shape can look a little different, longer or thinner, and invite looking again.
Invite counting the straight sides of each shape.
Suggest following each side with a finger and counting them aloud.
Suggest asking whether the shape is closed and has the right number of sides.
Count the sides aloud together, say how many the asked-for shape has, and point at the one that matches.
M-SHP-SIZE: Say that a big shape and a small shape can be the same shape, and invite looking again.
Invite ignoring how big each one is and looking only at its form.
Suggest picturing the small shape growing bigger, or the big one shrinking.
Suggest counting the sides and corners and ignoring the size.
Say that both are the same shape, one bigger and one smaller, and point at the one that was asked for.
M-SHP-SQRECT: Say that in a square all the sides are the same, and in a rectangle some are longer, and invite looking again.
Invite comparing the sides of each shape with a finger.
Suggest comparing the long side and the short side of each shape.
Suggest asking whether all four sides look the same length.
Compare the sides aloud: all the same for the square, long and short for the rectangle, and point at the right one.
M-SPACE-WORD: Invite the child to listen to the place word again and look at where the ball is.
Say the place word slowly and invite finding it in the picture.
Suggest acting it out with a real ball and a box or a table, and then looking at the pictures.
Suggest saying what is above, below, inside or next to what in each picture.
Say the place word slowly, point at where the ball is in the right picture, and invite the child to choose it.
M-PAT-COPY: Invite the child to look at the pattern from the first picture and put the same one in the first place.
Suggest putting a finger on each picture of the pattern in turn and finding the same one below.
Suggest saying the pattern aloud and then saying what goes in each place, one by one.
Suggest checking each place against the picture above it.
Point at the first picture of the pattern and the first place, say what goes there, and invite the child to do the next one.
M-SHARE-UNEQ: Say that sharing fairly means both friends get the same, and invite the child to look at how many each one has.
Invite counting what each friend has and comparing the two numbers.
Suggest giving one to this friend, then one to the other friend, in turn, until none are left.
Suggest dealing like cards, one for each in turn.
Deal the pictures one for each friend in turn together with the child, and then count what each has.
M-CS-OFF1: Invite the child to count the squares the robot has to cross, not counting the one it starts on.
Say that each step moves the robot to the next square, and invite following the way with a finger.
Suggest hopping along the squares with a finger, one hop for each step, and counting the hops.
Suggest comparing the number of steps with the number of squares between the robot and the flag.
Count the squares aloud together, starting with the first square after the robot, and point at the flag.
M-CNT-DECADE: Remind the child that after nine comes a new ten, and invite counting slowly together up to the nine.
Suggest saying the numbers softly and stopping just before the next ten.
Count aloud together to the nine of this ten, then pause and let the child say what comes next.
Suggest tapping the numbers on a number line while counting.
Say the number that follows and let the child repeat the last few numbers with you.
M-NUM-REV: Invite the child to look at the first digit and say how many tens it tells.
Suggest reading the number slowly, left to right, one digit at a time.
Suggest comparing the two numbers and asking which one is bigger.
Suggest building the number from ten and some ones.
Point at the first digit, say the number, and invite the child to find it again.
M-NUM-TEEN: Remind the child that a teen number is a ten and some more, and invite looking at the group again.
Suggest separating ten of the objects first.
Suggest circling ten objects and counting only the rest.
Suggest saying ten and then the ones, slowly.
Say that ten and these few make the number, and point at the ones that are left.
M-NL-SPACE: Invite the child to look at the jumps along the line and count each jump, not each mark.
Suggest starting on the number and not counting it.
Suggest touching the starting number, then hopping one step at a time while saying the numbers.
Suggest counting the small gaps between the marks.
Hop along the line together, step by step, and stop where the landing number is.
M-NL-DIR: Remind the child that the line runs from small to big, from the left to the right, and invite looking at the first number.
Suggest finding zero or the smallest number first.
Suggest reading the labelled numbers from the left, out loud.
Suggest following the arrow along the line.
Point to the left end, then walk along to the right together until the right number.
M-PART-MISS: Invite the child to look at how many there are altogether and how many are already in the basket.
Suggest asking what is left outside.
Suggest covering the ones in the basket and counting only the others.
Suggest counting up from the part to the whole.
Say the whole, say the part, and let the child count what is left.
M-EQ-OPER: Remind the child that the equals sign means both sides are the same, and invite checking each side.
Suggest working out each side by itself first.
Suggest looking at the scale: both pans must be the same.
Suggest saying the equal sign out loud as the same as.
Work out one side together, then the other, and compare the two numbers.
M-MEAS-BIG: Invite the child to guess and then look at the scale, because big does not always mean heavy.
Suggest imagining holding each one in a hand.
Suggest watching which side goes down, and noticing it is the heavier one.
Suggest comparing one stone with one feather.
Point at the side that is lower and say that lower means heavier.
M-CLOCK-HANDS: Remind the child that the short thick hand tells the hour, and invite finding it first.
Suggest asking which hand is shorter.
Suggest looking only at the short hand and saying which number it is near.
Suggest saying that the long hand is on twelve for a whole hour.
Point at the short hand and say the number it shows.
M-ADD-RECOUNT: Invite the child to start from the bigger number and count on from there.
Suggest not counting the first group again.
Suggest saying the first number and then counting on with the fingers, one at a time.
Suggest hiding the first group and remembering how many it was.
Say the first number and count on together, one at a time, to the answer.
M-COL-MIX: Invite the child to think what happens when two paints are mixed, and look at the two colours again.
Suggest remembering the colours of the rainbow.
Suggest imagining the two paints on a page, side by side, slowly mixing.
Suggest comparing with a mix the child already knows.
Say the two colours and the colour they make, and invite the child to find it.
M-COL-SHADE: Remind the child that a light colour and a dark colour can be the same colour, and invite looking at the colour itself.
Suggest ignoring how light it is.
Suggest asking whether it is blue or red or green, only that.
Suggest thinking of the sky and the sea, both blue.
Say the colour name, and point at the one that has the same name.
M-SHP-CLOSED: Invite the child to follow the edge with a finger and see if it closes all the way around.
Suggest checking that every side is straight.
Suggest tracing the edge slowly and noticing any opening or curved side.
Suggest asking if an ant could walk all the way around.
Trace the edge together and say whether it is closed and straight.
M-PAT-UNIT: Invite the child to find the small part that repeats and say it out loud.
Suggest reading the row from the left, slowly.
Suggest saying the first few pictures and noticing where they start again.
Suggest tapping each picture while saying its name.
Say the repeating part together, then point at the picture that breaks it.
M-PAT-GROW: Invite the child to notice that each tower grows by one cube, and look at the next one again.
Suggest counting the cubes of each tower.
Suggest counting the cubes of the tower before and adding one.
Suggest saying the numbers one after the other.
Count the cubes of the last tower together and add one more.
M-LOG-NOT: Remind the child that there are two clues, and the answer must fit both of them.
Suggest dealing with one clue at a time.
Suggest crossing out the ones that break the first clue, then checking the second clue.
Suggest saying the two clues out loud.
Say the first clue and put aside what does not fit, then the second, and point at what is left.
M-CS-FIXALL: Remind the child that only one step is wrong, and invite reading the steps one at a time.
Suggest comparing each step with the one that should come.
Suggest saying each step out loud and stopping at the one that is different.
Suggest comparing the steps in pairs.
Read the steps together until the different one, and point at it.
